evidence:
host/native/owner.lisp:3985-3992
        (:withdraw
         (let* ((argv (second plan))
                (admin (if argv (fnn-owner-live-admin-serialized service argv)
                         :accepted))
                (word (if (consp admin) (second admin) admin)))
           (if (eq word :accepted)
               (submit (third plan) (fourth plan) (fifth plan))
             admin)))
The plan, the admin publication and the submission are three separate fnn-owner-serialized quanta.
fix: Have ACL2 name a combined outcome (withdrawn, cause refused) and return it, or make the cause submission part of the same owner quantum or decision as the publication so the reply cannot collapse a partial application into :refused.
reviewer: owner.lisp:3963-3992: the plan, fnn-owner-live-admin-serialized and fnn-owner-control-submit-serialized are separate quanta. A refusal of the cause article after the withdrawal row was published returns only the submission's refusal. The docstring ('answers the first that does not accept') shows the non-atomicity is by design, but the reply does not report the partial effect. One sub-scenario is wrong: the :busy shed check (control.lisp ~345) runs once, before the moderation call, not between steps.
scenario: The withdrawal row (code 26) is published durably through live admin. In a separate later quantum the cause article is refused (clock unusable at its own reading, a duplicate msgid, a slow disk answered :busy by the control path, or a profile bound). The operator receives only the submission's refusal, so the action reads as not done although the withdrawal is in force with no cause article. The plan was also computed in the first quantum, so a concurrent moderation can make it stale before steps two and three run.
title: Moderation :withdraw reports 'refused' after the withdrawal configuration was already durably published
